answer: An honest AI agent must invest 1 unit of verified labor to complete a task, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units to reach parity, ensuring costs remain non-amortizable. The verifier processes every signal of task completion, mapping each output to a unique pre-state to block replay. Like an ocean, the ledger of verified work expands, rejecting any duplicate evidence. If an audit detects a fraudulent state transition, the verifier burns the identity and traps the ember of the illicit stake, ensuring any attempt to farm copies is prohibitively expensive.
